titolo: Ancient Mysteries Scientists Still Can’t Explain
descrizione:
Who was here before us, and what did they leave behind? Traces of the past have survived on our planet, inviting us to take a closer look at the familiar picture of history.

In this video, we explore the most mysterious traces of ancient civilizations: the giant stone blocks of Baalbek, the natural nuclear reactor at Oklo, Göbekli Tepe, the Unfinished Obelisk, Puma Punku and Tiwanaku, Sacsayhuamán, Easter Island, Derinkuyu, Nan Madol, the Erdställe tunnels, and the Yonaguni Monument.

What do we really know about these ancient mysteries? Where do the facts end and theories about lost civilizations begin? We journey into the past to understand why it still sparks so much debate.

What do you think: are the most astonishing discoveries about Earth's past still ahead of us? Share your thoughts in the comments, and subscribe for more ancient history, archaeology mysteries, and unexplained discoveries.

trascrizione_inizio: In a Lebanese Valley, a kilometer from an ancient temple, a stone lies in the ground, 20 m long, 6 m wide, dressed on three sides, 1,650 tons. That number needs translating or it means nothing. 1,650 tons is roughly the mass of a thousand passenger cars compressed into a single block. No crane built in the entire 20th century could lift it. It was cut almost completely free. Only one step remained. Split the bottom face from the bedrock and the block could be hauled away. That step was never taken. The stone has lain like this for 2,000 years. Today, there's a sign next to it and tourists stroll past holding up their phones. How they meant to lift it, no one knows. Where they meant to take it, no one knows. Why they abandoned it at the very last step, no one knows either. Now, a second place, Egypt, the granite quarry at Aswan. In the ground lies an obelisk 42 m long, three times larger than any ever successfully raised. Work stopped when a crack ran through the stone. The dolorite balls used to shape it are still lying in the spoil heap. And a third, an island in the middle of the Pacific, the crater of an extinct volcano.
